title: Default parameters
learningObjectives: Explain default parameters and write reusable JavaScript functions or control flow.

understand.concept: Default parameters provide a value when an argument is omitted or explicitly undefined. They do not apply when the argument is null, zero, false, or an empty string. Defaults are evaluated when the function is called and can reference earlier parameters.
understand.whyItMatters: Defaults simplify optional inputs, but they should match the domain meaning. Do not accidentally replace valid values such as zero with a truthy fallback expression.
understand.analogy: A default parameter is a prepared value used when the caller leaves an input slot empty.
understand.analogyLimit: The analogy is simplified; JavaScript execution, hoisting, and parameter evaluation follow language rules.

explain.narrative: The omitted and undefined arguments use the default. null is passed through and becomes the value of name.

examples.explanation: The omitted and undefined arguments use the default. null is passed through and becomes the value of name.
examples.expectedOutput: The browser console displays the function or control-flow result described.

practise.guidedTask: Create a function with two default parameters. Test omitted, undefined, null, zero, and empty string arguments.
practise.independentTask: Create a small program that uses the control structure or function concept. Test normal, boundary, and optional-input cases.
hints: Keep inputs explicit and return results where practical.

practice.starterCode:
<!doctype html>
<html lang="en"><head><meta charset="utf-8"><meta name="viewport" content="width=device-width, initial-scale=1"><title>Default parameters</title></head><body>
<script>function greet(name='Learner'){return `Hello, ${name}`;}console.log(greet());console.log(greet('Asha'));console.log(greet(undefined));console.log(greet(null));</script>
</body></html>

questions.prompt: When does a default parameter value apply?
options: When the argument is omitted or undefined
questions.answer: When the argument is omitted or undefined
questions.explanation: Default parameter initializers apply when no argument is supplied or the value is undefined.

questions.prompt: What makes a function easier to reuse and test?
options: Clear inputs, focused responsibility, and explicit results
Hidden global state and unrelated side effects
A very long function with many unrelated tasks
questions.answer: Clear inputs, focused responsibility, and explicit results
questions.explanation: Focused functions with clear inputs and outputs are easier to reason about and test.
